title: Bhartrihari's Vakyapadiya
author: bhartrhari
attributionNote: By Bhartrihari, the grammarian and philosopher. The second book appears to have lost part of its middle in transmission, and the commentary on the work is not part of this text.
description: The Vakyapadiya argues that language is not a tool the mind uses but the substance of what is known: a word is an indivisible unit that appears to be analysed into parts, meaning arises in the sentence rather than the word, and behind grammar stands the same reality the Vedanta calls brahman. Its first book sets out the doctrine of the word-principle in verse; the second and third work through the categories of time, substance and negation.
historicalContext: The chief work of the school of grammar as a philosophy, and the source of the doctrine that all knowledge is shot through with language that the later Kashmirian Shaiva authors took over. It is read both as grammar's account of its own object and as a metaphysics.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: 1,997 units of the three khandas, streamed at read time one section at a time. The e-text numbers the verses in a mixed scheme, so some sections are addressed by khanda and samuddesha and others by khanda alone; the reader follows the file.
